requirement:
Each first-party Rust file under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` MUST have at least 80%
execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the
file-and-line union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`;
a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated
child processes has a positive execution count for it.

The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception
evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage. A file established to
contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST
NOT require a threshold exception.
Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file
contains no executable coverage obligations.
rationale:
I judged this from the supplied test sources only. I did not request implementation source. The reviewed tests cover each obligation of `requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`, and their assertions enforce the expected outcomes.

- **80% per file, exact counts, no averaging, no per-function target.**
  - `exact_per_file_threshold_and_partial_functions` checks `threshold(79_999, 100_000)` fails even though it displays as 80.0%. It checks `80_000/100_000` passes, `0/0` fails, and a report at exactly 4/5 (80.0%) passes.
  - The same test fails `driver.rs` at 0/1 and at 7/10 (70%). Both failures happen while `code.rs` is at 100%, and the 7/10 case is annotated "the 85% average … cannot rescue driver.rs", so the file percentages are not averaged.
  - `a_function_below_eighty_percent_needs_no_exception_when_its_file_passes` has a function at 1/3 inside a file at 10/12 (83.3%). The report passes with no "Accepted exceptions" section, so no 80% target applies per function.
- **Union counting across processes, child processes and filtered runs.** `children_and_filtered_runs_contribute_to_the_same_union` splits line coverage between a parent process and a child process, so only the union reaches 5/5. A later all-zero filtered attempt does not erase the earlier execution.
- **Freshness, selection and active build configuration.**
  - `stale_missing_legacy_and_uncertain_history_cannot_use_older_success` covers stale source, missing or unreadable coverage, records without function attribution, an excluded other-configuration record, and corrupt run metadata. In each case the report excludes the data or flags it.
  - In `accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution`, a covered record from an earlier configuration is not combined into a later configuration. The result is "code.rs: not measured", not "1/1".
- **Exceptions for unmet thresholds.**
  - `accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution` shows an accepted file exception lets the file pass at 0/1 while the zero-execution function still fails. It also shows a rejected review (`determination is false`) and a `{fixme}` determination do not count as accepted.
  - `missing_and_stale_explanations_fail_the_report` covers a missing citation review and a changed citation or outline input.
  - `function_explanations_never_transfer_to_other_functions_or_the_file` covers exceptions not excusing other functions or the file.
- **Unmeasured files need an exception and get no fabricated percentage.** Several tests produce "code.rs: not measured — FAIL" or "not measured — accepted exception". `accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution` also asserts the output does not contain "code.rs: 0/".
- **Files with no executable obligations.** `unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear` uses `struct S; trait T { fn declaration(); }` and asserts "no executable obligations — pass" with the report passing. `default_trait_bodies_and_cfg_exclusions_are_obligations_but_declarations_are_not` adds `inventory` checks that declarations, macro calls and derived structs are not obligations.
- **No lines recorded does not mean no obligations.** The same test rewrites the file to `fn missing() {}` with no recorded lines. The report says "not measured — FAIL" and `#fn[missing]: not measured`. A trait body and a `#[cfg(any())]` function are also treated as obligations.
- **Parse failures.** The same test checks that a parse failure is reported and the report fails.

The cited requirements are context only. I found no untested obligation, wrong expected result or weak assertion. There are no {fixme} acknowledgments.

Each first-party Rust file under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` MUST have at least 80%
execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the
file-and-line union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`;
a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated
child processes has a positive execution count for it.
The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception
evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage. A file established to
contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST
NOT require a threshold exception.
Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file
contains no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file: every `.rs` file among the sources reference discovery considers under {cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except those under the project-root `vendor` directory. Each explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and each struct, enum, and union is an item that can be covered. An item is covered when it has a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example, or a valid citation of the built-in `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`, in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body; or when its outline node, or an outline node containing it, is recorded with its current hash as an outline input of an evidence record, a citation review, or a site review. Outline inputs recorded from selected search snippets under {cite}`requirements.authoring.finish_search.inputs` MUST count alongside mandatory inputs and additional reads. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file. Only {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples` make an uncovered item a validation error; other items without recent coverage are warned about under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report`.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
:::{req} index.summary
The coverage index MUST display the combined view selected under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. It MUST show the number of
selected test attempts and summarize coverage excluded because it is stale,
unavailable, or from a historical build configuration. Detailed test identities,
run provenance, and per-test execution data MUST remain in the saved coverage
artifacts rather than being included in the generated book.
For first-party Rust files under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, the summary MUST compute
line coverage from the union of instrumented file-and-line locations in the
selected fresh records, including their associated child-process records.
Each location MUST count once in the denominator and count as covered when any
selected record has a positive execution count for it. Percentages MUST be
computed from those union counts rather than averaged across process reports.
A view with no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable. The index
MUST visibly identify incomplete coverage and MUST NOT imply that every current
test has coverage merely because all available records are valid.
:::{req} index.selection
The coverage index MUST combine the most recent recorded test attempt for each
nextest binary and test name among the retained runs. "Most recent" MUST refer
to when the attempt started, including failed or interrupted attempts. A newer
filtered run MUST update only the tests it executes, leaving other compatible
test records available to the combined view. A newer attempt with missing or
unreadable coverage MUST be shown as unavailable rather than replaced with an
older successful attempt. Results from incompatible instrumented build
configurations MUST NOT be combined under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration`.
The main combined view MUST use the instrumented build configuration of the
most recently started recorded test attempt. Latest-per-test selection MUST
occur within that configuration. Records from other configurations MUST be
identified as excluded historical coverage. Configuration selection MUST use
recorded metadata without building or executing tests.
:::{req} index.freshness
Only records whose captured source inputs match the current project source and
whose build configurations are compatible MAY contribute execution counts to
the combined view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`.
Records invalidated by a source change, or whose compatibility cannot be
established, MUST be identified as stale or unavailable and excluded from the
combined coverage totals. Their per-process reports and matching captured source
MUST remain retained in the build artifacts until those artifacts are removed.
